reviews.review:
Souls games are my bread and butter and this fits nicely in the middle of my experiences with the genre. a solid AA offering, albeit with a fairly steep learning curve as far as "builds" go. it's pretty unbalanced and a lot of the weapons that seem like theyd be high damage or great aoe tools all just felt weak and slow. smgs have better accuracy and dps than assault rifles. the shotguns barely outshoot pistols (which boast a longer range) and sniper rifles are dope. most classes feel pretty useless and like you arent leveling up the right stuff until its been 4 hours of banging your head against the wall. its a picky game, but if you kind of break the builds a bit the game really has great level design. the "spiderweb" map that souls games are known for are some of the better ones ive seen. there was even a wrap around that was basically a troll. i got a good laugh out of some random moments. a little janky and chuggy at times. graphics are middling. the enviroments are fairly plain but varied enough to keep me from getting lost. the game really hits its stride after the second world imo. the exp gained didnt scale well with the levels, and then all of a sudden you're blowing through levels and get a respec to change to any single powerhouse type build to run through the rest of the game with. the bosses are fairly easy, as they have smaller hp pool than id expect, but the range and variety of the battles kept me entertained. a few of them have a few one shot/unfair punishment moves but with practice, as with all souls games, much fun can be had here. if you enjoyed mortal shell, its closest to that, mixed with some gunplay from remnant (but not over ran with gank/group bosses, yay!).
i wish it had co-op but its been a blast so far. the learning curve never kept me down, and its much much more strategic than i initially thought. careful planning is key and get ready to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ die. have fun!

Only buy this if you're a diehard fan of the "soulslike" game formula. There are much better middleware titles in this genre that are worth picking up before this one such as Hellpoint, Mortal Shell, Thymesia, Lords of the Fallen, The Surge 1/2 and Remnant: From the Ashes just to name a few.

If that warning didn't dissuade you then in short what you are getting is Dark Souls meets Destiny. That sounds like a recipe for a big macho combo winner of a game right? Well there are some problems.

First off let's get it out of the way: while the graphics aren't technically all that bad, the game is just ugly. Maybe it's just me but the art style doesn't work well for what they were trying to accomplish with the setting and story. It's like they wanted to make a dark gothic horror game in space, but they slapped glowy lights over everything and on top of that added an intense bloom effect. Then after realizing the game was too colorful, they put a filter over it to try to wash out the image a bit. The result is a low contrast visual mess. It doesn't help that the Shadows setting specifically has to be kept on Low, as High or even Medium brought my more than capable PC to a crawl (40-50 fps on High, 144 fps on Low).

Secondly a lot of the systems in this game just aren't all that polished. In particular coming up with a character build that makes sense ends up being somewhat of a challenge because of how the attribute requirements work for the weapons. Most weapons scale primarily off of something called "Normal Scaling" which is gained via increasing the Expertise attribute. This attribute also increases your health pool by a small amount (as all attributes do) and boosts the effectiveness of healing items. Sounds good, right? Like you would probably want to put a lot of points into this. Well, the problem is that most of the weapons in the game do not require Expertise in order to actually equip them; rather they need points in other attributes, some of which do absolutely nothing for your particular build. What if you want to use a shotgun as a backup weapon? Better pump up that Strength stat, which increases melee damage and therefore is doing nothing for you if you don't care about having better melee attacks.

This lack of refinement of the game systems also applies to the combat. The controls don't always feel all that responsive. There were times when I really needed to get a heal off or dodge an attack and despite mashing the corresponding button, my character just would not perform the action. Furthermore, locking on to enemies Dark Souls style is pretty important because it allows you to circle around your target and get behind them to attack their weak spot, but this also results in missing shots, because none of the weapons are hitscan and you need to lead if the target is moving. Speaking of getting behind enemies, most encounters with tougher opponents result in you ridiculously spinning around them as you bait certain attacks out, because hitting those weak spots is really important. The gulf between amount of damage some enemies take in their weak spot (usually on their back) versus hitting them in say, for example, the chest, is huge. Think 10x or even 20x damage huge depending the weapon you're using and whether or not you increased the Precision stat, which increases Critical damage. These endless "circle danaces" aren't fun.

On a more positive note the game's lore and overall story is passable, the character dialogue is well written (albeit there isn't much of it) and the English voice acting is good. This culminates in an ending that is pretty damn weird though. I don't want to spoil it, suffice to say there is a twist you probably won't see coming, and you'll either love it or hate it.

In summary life is too short to be wasted on games this mediocre. But, if you really want to try this one out: it is playable, it is beatable, and it only crashed 3 or 4 times on me.

For better visuals and performance I suggest the following:
* Set Shadows to Low in the in-game advanced graphics options menu. Other settings can be maxed out.
* Turn TAA off in the config file.
* [nVidia users]Turn sharpening on in the nVidia control panel, somewhere between 15-35%.
* [nVidia users] Set Low Latency mode to Ultra in the nVidia control panel.
Awesome soulslike with a few progression issues. Sniper rifles for headshots are rly fun.
